answer.direct_calls: Every one of the 63 consumer bodies is called directly, and only directly: 67 verified `call rel32` sites in 65 FDE caller bodies, no direct jumps, and no indirect path -- no relocation addend, no stored copy, no immediate, no rip-relative reference, and no dynamic symbol names a consumer start.
answer.families: The 36 callers of the 36 uniform 1169-byte consumers all use the flag-pair template: two stack flag bytes are zeroed, rdi and rsi point at them, rdx takes a rip-relative static, and the return value is tested against null. 28 further sites pass a rip-relative static in rsi as the second argument. The remaining 3 sites -- the two callers of 0x5a79730 and the caller of 0x5cf4540 -- match neither pattern.
answer.pairing: 64 of the 65 caller bodies call exactly one consumer; the single exception, body 0x2b41b70, calls three (0x2b3aba0, 0x2b3b3e0, 0x2b3d250). Three consumers have more than one caller: 0x2e8e7b0 has three call sites and 0x2b3c9d0 and 0x5a79730 have two each.

boundaries.one_level_up: For each caller body this packet records only two counts: raw direct rel32 call/jump byte occurrences in .text whose target is the body start, and .rela.dyn entries whose addend is the body start. Who reads the seven stored pointers, and the callers' callers in general, are outside this packet's question.
boundaries.prior_packets: RE-005-node115-x5-caller-slot-consumers (#3235) pins the 63 consumer bodies and records only the count of each consumer's direct rel32 callers; this packet enumerates them. Individual sites appear incidentally in earlier work: RE-017 packets record 11 of the sites as transfer/call rows (0x2b4261c, 0x4e359fc, 0x4e35c7c, 0x4e36191, 0x4e3642f, 0x4e45a61, 0x4e460c1, 0x4e46e71, 0x4e47938, 0x4e47cdf, 0x4e4a771), RE-011-evm-fee-history-115 records one call row (site 0x2a0afd5 into 0x2b3daa0), and RE-012-node115-startup-end-height's instruction window over caller body 0x2b41b70 includes its three sites (0x2b420da, 0x2b4261c, 0x2b428ab). No earlier packet enumerates the call sites of the consumer set, groups them by caller body, pins their call-site conditions, or excludes the indirect reference forms for the consumers.
boundaries.runtime_behaviour: Which runtime path reaches a given call site, what the per-site statics name, and the concrete Rust types of the caller bodies are not established by static evidence.

flag_pair.definition: Within the eight instructions before the call at least two `mov byte ptr [rsp + k], 0` stores zero a pair of stack flag bytes; within six instructions a `lea rdx, [rip + disp]` loads a static as the third argument; the instruction after the call is `test rax, rax`.

residual.definition: Neither pattern: the two callers of the large consumer 0x5a79730 and the caller of 0x5cf4540; each site is pinned with its own preceding and following instruction.

static_second_argument.definition: Within six instructions before the call a `lea rsi, [rip + disp]` loads a static as the second argument, and the site is not in the flag-pair family.

one_level_up.note: Every caller body with zero direct rel32 callers has exactly one .rela.dyn entry whose addend is its start; those stored pointers are counted, not followed.

question: Who calls the 63 consumers of GOT slot 0x64e7718 directly -- from which caller bodies and call sites, under what call-site conditions -- and is there any indirect path to a consumer body?

source.note: The consumer set is re-derived from the binary in analyze() and checked against the start, end, and body hash pinned by the source packet.
